full_judgment: 10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner then contended that the appellate court erroneously threw the burden of proof upon the defendants and as such it came to an erroneous decision which is liable to be set aside. I have perused the judgment of the appellate court and find that it started with the assumption that as the defendants have failed to prove their case, it must be held that the plaintiffs case has been proved. At the time of consideration of title of the plaintiff the appellate court failed to consider as to why the plaintiff did not produce any single rent receipt to show payment of rent for the suit land. The appellate court also failed to consider that the defendants have produced rent receipts, Ext. Band B1, granted by the ex-landlord and Exts. B-B4, granted by the Government. The appellate court thus without considering Exts. B series abruptly came to the finding that the defendants are not in possession of the suit land reversing the finding of the trial court regaling possession of the suit land. I think this finding is not sustainable in law.
